questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an english talkning country and I had wanted to experience the Australian culture for a long time. Besides that a lot of the australian universities work on a high academic level which was very important for me as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information upon arrival and Monash University was very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I just asked people at the university for help and 9 ou of 10 times they knew the answer and could help me 
immediately

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quit difficult due to the housing crisis that is happening in Melbourne at the moment. I recommend that you use facebook groups such as Fairyfloss and that you are patient because you will find a home eventually

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is the BEST! You really get to experience what it feels like to be living in another city and get that local experience. It is very easy to find friends and people to talk to even when you don't live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved my apartment and the area that I lived in but it didn't have anything to do with me being a student. I don't think there were a lot of housing available for students (at least not any that wasn't extremely expensive)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it a bit difficult in the beginning, but once you got the hang of it, it wasn't difficult at all

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I found some courses in the handbook online which I applied for and if they were available I was assigned to a class. In Australia they have many different timeslots for the same class so I was able to pick and choose the day and at what time I wanted the particular class. 

I had four different classes but upon arrival I learned that I did not have the skills to participate in one of the classes - luckily I was able to change course immediatly with help from my university

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email my host university and get help and they would answer asap

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was super successful. There were one class that I could not sign up for but other than that I got everything I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a list of all the courses you want and get as many as possible aprowed by KU. The course might sound interesting when you ready about it but could be completely different in real life. Therefore it is nice to have courses you can choose instead.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four courses and I must say that the academic level was lower than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I had one lecture a week in each course which was a small video that I watched on Moodle (equal to Absalon) and then I had one tutorial in each course where I had to show up. 

At KU I'm used to working on a project and then end it with an exam where at Monash I didn't have any exams but I had a lot (and I mean a lot) of assignments through the semester which counted towards the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Practise of Journalism
- Introduction to Television Studies 
- Public Relation Strategy 
- Broadcast Studio Journalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really loved Broadcast Studio Journalism because it was very hands on and the teacher was fantastic

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Mostly alcohol and eating out. And also different trips I ended up going on. 

My personal spending and food pr. month changed so it is difficult for me to set a specific price.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The only thing that was less expensive that I expected was take away coffee - otherwise everything else was more expensive. Especially vegetables at the grocery store was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use any non-academic opportunities at my uni but they were there and seemed great

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fitness, different sports activities and other social clubs such as surfing etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would participate in all the exchange activities that's there. It's a great way to meet other exchange students thats in the same position as yourself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore the city and all its cultural activities. I also rented a car and went down on the great ocean road, camped through victoria, saw Wilsons Promentory and travveled up the east coast after my semester finished.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy - the culture is not that different from the danish one

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it a bit difficult to be honest - but I tried to be super open and asked if they would like to drink a coffee before class or something like that

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: hat the Australien people are so chill, helpfull, and kind. I have never experienced anything like that

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it because time will fly by so fast!
2. It is okay to have a bad day and not do anything (even though you want to experience everything while your there)
3. Prioritize uni but remember that exchange is much more than that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the people that I got to meet and form friendships with and also just getting to live in another city. It was a nice way to challenge myself

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a new city and have to learn and build everything up from scratch

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
